senses.gloss: The act or skill of hitting the ball in baseball.
examples: His *batting* has improved a lot since spring training.
The team's *batting* fell apart in the second half of the season.
She leads the league in *batting* this year.

senses.gloss: A long, hard struggle against a problem or an opponent.
examples: She lost her *battle* with cancer last spring.
The company faces a legal *battle* over the patent.
Getting my kids to eat vegetables is a daily *battle*.

senses.gloss: A separate section or compartment of a building, ship, or vehicle.
examples: The truck backed up to the loading *bay*.
All three service *bays* at the garage were full.
The injured sailor was carried down to the sick *bay*.

senses.gloss: A person or thing that gives other people hope or guidance.
examples: The clinic became a *beacon* of hope for the whole valley.
Her third-grade teacher was a *beacon* in a hard year.
The paper was long seen as a *beacon* of free speech.

senses.gloss: A small drop of liquid on a surface.
examples: *Beads* of sweat stood out on his forehead.
A *bead* of water rolled down the cold glass.
*Beads* of dew clung to the grass at dawn.

senses.gloss: A line of light shining out from something.
examples: The flashlight's *beam* swept across the yard.
A *beam* of sunlight came through the kitchen window.
The truck's high *beams* blinded me for a second.

senses.gloss: The direction of one place from another, or your sense of where you are.
examples: The pilot took a *bearing* on the lighthouse.
Give me a *bearing* and a distance and I'll find it.
It took me a minute to get my *bearings* in the new building.

senses.gloss: Influence on or relevance to something.
examples: His age has no *bearing* on the decision.
That letter has a direct *bearing* on the case.
The weather had little *bearing* on the outcome.

senses.gloss: The area a police officer patrols or the subject a reporter regularly covers.
examples: Two officers walk this *beat* every evening.
She covers the education *beat* for the local paper.
He spent twenty years as a cop on the *beat*.

senses.gloss: An area of ground prepared for growing plants.
examples: She planted tulips in the *bed* by the front door.
The vegetable *beds* need weeding again.
We built raised *beds* out of cedar boards.

senses.gloss: The bottom of a river, lake, or sea.
examples: By August the river *bed* was nothing but cracked mud.
The drought exposed the *bed* of the reservoir.
The wreck still lies on the *bed* of the lake.

senses.gloss: A gathering where people compete at something or work together.
examples: She won the school spelling *bee* two years running.
The neighbors held a quilting *bee* in the church hall.
Our town still has a sewing *bee* every winter.

senses.gloss: The state of existing.
examples: The company came into *being* in a garage in 1978.
The treaty brought a new nation into *being*.
No one can say how the universe came into *being*.

senses.gloss: A hollow metal object that makes a ringing sound when it is struck.
examples: The church *bells* rang at noon.
He tied a small *bell* to the cat's collar.
A *bell* over the shop door jingled as we walked in.

senses.gloss: A loop of rubber or metal that carries things or turns parts inside a machine.
examples: The mechanic replaced a cracked fan *belt*.
Boxes came down the conveyor *belt* one at a time.
A worn *belt* was making the dryer squeal.

senses.gloss: A long stretch of land known for one particular feature.
examples: Corn grows across a wide *belt* of the Midwest.
The storm hit the coastal *belt* hardest.
He grew up in the farm *belt* of central Illinois.

senses.gloss: The seat where substitute players wait, or the substitutes themselves.
examples: He spent most of the season on the *bench*.
Our *bench* is deeper than theirs this year.
The coach cleared the *bench* in the last minute.

senses.gloss: A judge's place in court, or judges taken as a group.
examples: The lawyers were called to approach the *bench*.
She served on the federal *bench* for twenty years.
The *bench* has ruled against the city twice.

senses.gloss: A long, sturdy table for working with tools or materials.
examples: He clamped the board to the *bench* and started sanding.
Her tools were laid out neatly on the *bench*.
The engine sat on a *bench* at the back of the shop.

senses.gloss: A good result or advantage that something brings.
examples: Walking every day has real health *benefits*.
The main *benefit* of the new system is speed.
Neither side saw much *benefit* in another meeting.

senses.gloss: An event held to raise money for a person or cause.
examples: The band played a *benefit* for the food bank.
Tickets to the *benefit* sold out in a day.
She organizes a *benefit* every fall for the animal shelter.

senses.gloss: A place at a dock where a ship ties up.
examples: The freighter pulled into its *berth* just after dawn.
Every *berth* at the marina was taken.
The ship left its *berth* an hour late.

senses.gloss: A place in a competition or on a team that a player or club earns.
examples: A win tonight clinches a playoff *berth*.
The team earned a *berth* in the national tournament.
She lost her *berth* on the Olympic squad after the injury.

senses.gloss: A choice or course of action that is likely to work well.
examples: Your best *bet* is to take the train.
A used sedan is a safer *bet* on that budget.
Calling ahead is a good *bet* on holidays.

senses.gloss: A book treated as the most trusted guide to a subject.
examples: That manual is the *bible* of home wiring.
Her cookbook became the *bible* for a generation of bakers.
For serious birders, this guide is the *bible*.

senses.gloss: An attempt to win or achieve something.
senses.ru: попытка добиться; заявка (на пост, на проведение)
examples: She announced a *bid* for a second term.
The city's *bid* to host the games failed.
His *bid* for a promotion went nowhere.

senses.gloss: A motorcycle, in everyday speech.
examples: He rode his *bike* all the way from Nevada.
There were a dozen *bikes* parked outside the bar.
She sold the *bike* and bought a pickup.

senses.gloss: The physical makeup and workings of a living thing.
examples: Human *biology* has not changed much in ten thousand years.
Researchers are studying the *biology* of the tumor.
Her *biology* made the medication risky.

senses.gloss: The light feathered object hit back and forth in badminton.
examples: The *birdie* landed just inside the line.
He served the *birdie* high over the net.
We lost the *birdie* in the hedge.

senses.gloss: The beginning or origin of something.
examples: New Orleans saw the *birth* of jazz.
The strike marked the *birth* of the union.
The *birth* of the internet changed everything.

senses.gloss: A chess piece that moves diagonally across the board.
examples: She moved her *bishop* to threaten the queen.
He traded a knight for a *bishop*.
A *bishop* can only stay on squares of one color.

senses.gloss: A piece of food taken into the mouth at one time, or a quick small meal.
examples: He took a *bite* of the sandwich and made a face.
Let's grab a *bite* before the movie.
There wasn't a *bite* of food left in the house.

senses.gloss: A single long narrow leaf of grass.
examples: Not a *blade* of grass grew in the shade.
A single *blade* stuck to his wet shoe.
Dew sat on every *blade* in the yard.

senses.gloss: One of the flat arms of a fan, propeller, or oar that pushes air or water.
examples: The helicopter's *blades* began to turn.
Dust had built up on the fan *blades*.
He dipped the *blade* of the paddle into the water.

senses.gloss: A cartridge that makes a bang but fires no bullet.
examples: The starter's pistol was loaded with *blanks*.
The soldiers fired *blanks* during the rehearsal.
A *blank* can still hurt you at close range.

senses.gloss: A thick layer of something that covers a wide area.
examples: A *blanket* of snow covered the fields.
Fog lay like a *blanket* over the harbor.
A *blanket* of ash settled on the parked cars.

senses.gloss: A very enjoyable time.
examples: We had a *blast* at the lake.
The party was a *blast*.
Her birthday trip was an absolute *blast*.

senses.gloss: A sudden loud sound from a horn, whistle, or instrument.
examples: A *blast* from the ship's horn made us jump.
Three short *blasts* of the whistle meant trouble.
The band opened with a *blast* of trumpets.

senses.gloss: Something that spoils or ruins a place or situation.
examples: Empty factories left decades of urban *blight*.
Litter is a *blight* on the whole neighborhood.
The city has a plan to fight *blight* downtown.

senses.gloss: A hidden shelter used by hunters or bird watchers.
examples: They were sitting in a duck *blind* before sunrise.
The photographer built a *blind* near the nest.
We waited in the *blind* for three hours and saw nothing.

senses.gloss: A small flashing dot on a radar or monitor screen.
examples: A *blip* appeared at the edge of the radar screen.
The *blip* vanished as the plane dropped low.
Each *blip* on the monitor matched a heartbeat.

senses.gloss: A solid piece of hard material with flat sides.
examples: He carved the bird out of a *block* of wood.
A *block* of ice sat melting in the cooler.
The wall is built of concrete *blocks*.

senses.gloss: Something that stops movement or progress.
examples: She has had a mental *block* about math since third grade.
There's a *block* somewhere in the drain.
Fear can be a real *block* to learning.

senses.gloss: A group or quantity of things handled together.
examples: The school bought a *block* of tickets for the show.
I set aside a *block* of time every morning to write.
A *block* of seats was reserved for the family.

senses.gloss: Family origin, or relatives you are descended from.
examples: They're related by *blood*, not by marriage.
There's Irish *blood* on my mother's side.
The land passes to his nearest relative by *blood*.

senses.gloss: A feeling of sadness or low spirits.
examples: She gets the *blues* every February.
A long walk usually cures my Monday *blues*.
New mothers often struggle with the baby *blues*.

senses.gloss: An attempt to fool someone by pretending you will do something.
examples: His threat to quit was just a *bluff*.
She called his *bluff* and he backed down.
The whole demand turned out to be a *bluff*.

senses.gloss: A stretch of time that you cannot remember clearly.
senses.ru: смутное воспоминание, время как в тумане
examples: The first month with a newborn was a total *blur*.
The whole trip is a *blur* now.
Everything after the crash is a *blur*.

senses.gloss: A reddening of the face caused by embarrassment.
examples: A *blush* spread across her cheeks.
He felt a *blush* rising as everyone turned to look.
The compliment brought a deep *blush* to his face.

senses.gloss: A long fluffy scarf made of feathers.
examples: She wore a pink feather *boa* to the party.
The costume came with a *boa* and long gloves.
*Boas* and sequins filled the dressing room.

senses.gloss: A dead person.
examples: Hikers found a *body* at the bottom of the ravine.
The *body* was identified from dental records.
Two *bodies* were recovered from the wreck.

senses.gloss: An organized group of people acting together officially.
examples: The governing *body* meets twice a year.
The student *body* voted on the new rules.
An independent *body* will review the complaints.

senses.gloss: A large mass or collection of something.
examples: The lake is the largest *body* of water in the state.
There's a growing *body* of evidence on the subject.
Her *body* of work spans forty years.

senses.gloss: A painful red swelling on the skin caused by infection.
examples: A *boil* on his neck kept him home from work.
The doctor lanced the *boil* and cleaned it out.
*Boils* often form where clothing rubs the skin.

senses.gloss: A flash of lightning.
examples: A *bolt* struck the tree in our yard.
*Bolts* of lightning lit up the whole valley.
The news hit him like a *bolt* out of the blue.

senses.gloss: A large roll of cloth.
examples: She bought a whole *bolt* of blue cotton.
*Bolts* of fabric leaned against the shop wall.
One *bolt* was enough for all the curtains.

senses.gloss: A sliding metal bar that fastens a door.
examples: He slid the *bolt* across the door.
The old barn door has a rusty *bolt*.
She drew back the *bolt* and looked outside.

senses.gloss: A complete failure, especially a movie or a show.
examples: The film was a *bomb* at the box office.
His first restaurant was a *bomb*.
The season opener turned out to be a total *bomb*.

senses.gloss: A person who sets off a bomb.
examples: The *bomber* was arrested two days later.
Police say the *bomber* acted alone.
The *bombers* left the package near the entrance.

senses.gloss: A close connection or feeling between people.
examples: There's a strong *bond* between the two sisters.
Years of training created a *bond* among the crew.
The *bond* between mother and child forms early.

senses.gloss: Money paid to a court so an arrested person can go free until trial.
examples: The judge set *bond* at fifty thousand dollars.
His family posted *bond* that same night.
She was released on *bond* the next morning.

senses.gloss: A record of the money a business takes in and pays out, usually in the plural.
examples: An accountant goes over the *books* every quarter.
The restaurant's *books* were a mess.
He was accused of cooking the *books*.

senses.gloss: A deep loud sound.
examples: The *boom* of thunder rattled the windows.
We heard the *boom* of fireworks across the river.
A sonic *boom* startled the whole town.

senses.gloss: A long movable pole that holds a microphone or the bottom edge of a sail.
examples: Duck, the *boom* is swinging around!
The sound man held the *boom* just out of frame.
A gust threw the *boom* hard to the left.

senses.gloss: A metal clamp locked onto a car's wheel so it cannot be driven away.
examples: The city put a *boot* on my car for unpaid tickets.
It costs a hundred dollars to get the *boot* taken off.
There was a bright yellow *boot* on the front tire.

senses.gloss: A restaurant table with high padded seats along the sides.
examples: We asked for a *booth* by the window.
The diner has six *booths* and a long counter.
He slid into the *booth* across from me.

senses.gloss: A small enclosed space where one person does something.
examples: She stepped into the voting *booth* and closed the curtain.
The old phone *booth* is still on the corner.
Buy your tickets at the *booth* by the gate.
